A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mix-LN research, and their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable. Ambiguities in two added v2 tables limit their interpretation but do not prevent comparison of the shared work.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre-training, fine-tuning, RLHF, vision, and layer-effectiveness experiments, including normalization compatibility results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Sections 2, 4–5 and Appendix B, independently of the ambiguities in its added tables.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same procedure: Post-LN in the initial fraction of layers and Pre-LN thereafter. The added LNS tables do not document an adaptation of Mix-LN; Appendix C attributes LayerNorm Scaling to separate work.

E1.justification: The explicitly named datasets and tasks remain unchanged, including C4, Commonsense170K, ultrafeedback, ImageNet-1K, and the downstream benchmarks. However, new Tables 2–3 identify no evaluation corpus, preventing determination of whether their results expand data coverage. Additional model names alone do not establish new tasks.

E2.justification: Direct Mix-LN comparisons retain the same comparators, including Pre-LN, Post-LN, DeepNorm, Admin, Group-LN, and Sandwich-LN. New Tables 2–3 compare Pre-LN with Pre-LN + LNS but contain no Mix-LN results, so they do not establish an additional comparator evaluated against Mix-LN.

E3.justification: v2 adds a reported Qwen2.5-0.5B evaluation configuration in Table 3 and additional 1B/7B configurations in Table 2, whose OLMO caption conflicts with its LLaMA rows. Existing protocols and Appendix A settings remain unchanged. The new tables lack sufficient settings for direct comparison with earlier experiments.

E4.justification: The Post-LN ratio sweep, representation-distance analyses, gradient and pruning analyses, and Appendix B initialization/embedding experiments are retained unchanged. The new scaling caveats are not accompanied by a documented additional sensitivity or robustness study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for the experimental comparisons. Averaging angular distance over 256K tokens is documented identically in both versions.

E6.justification: v2 Tables 2–3 add Pre-LN/Pre-LN + LNS perplexity pairs: 23.14/21.99 and 16.06/14.98 for rows labeled LLaMA-1B/7B, and 20.62/19.57 for Qwen2.5-0.5B. Table 2 instead names OLMO in its caption. These are added entries, not demonstrated changes in Mix-LN performance under matched settings. Existing numerical results remain unchanged; Section 4.2 newly reports increased sensitivity at 7B.

T1.justification: Equation (7) changes the LayerNorm Jacobian reduction from an exact equality to an approximation, qualifying its mathematical status. The surrounding assumptions and derivation remain unchanged, with no new proof or approximation-error analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims about Pre-LN causing ineffective deeper layers and Mix-LN improving training and downstream learning without increasing model size.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 removes the expectation that early training advantages generally persist and adds sensitivity to the Post-LN fraction and warm-up at 7B. New Section 6 explicitly identifies instability beyond 7B, conjectures a connection to Post-LN, and proposes mitigation as future work.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 adds qualitative guidance that larger-scale training requires longer warm-up. Its highlighted 6.25% Post-LN fraction was already disclosed in v1 Appendix A, so this is not a new setting. The detailed hyperparameter table and code-access information remain unchanged, and no precise protocol accompanies the added LNS tables.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Jaiswal et al. (2024), Huang et al. (2025), Sun et al. (2025), and Liu et al.'s random-pruning work. Brief additions discuss normalization-related spikes and position Sun et al.'s LayerNorm Scaling as building on this paper. Most existing related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Section 6 to Appendix C; Limitations and Acknowledgment sections are added. Section 4.2 is locally rewritten, and author affiliations and conference headers are updated. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds two small perplexity tables, relocates Figures 5–6 and several retained tables through reflow, and updates table numbering. Author formatting, conference headers, link colors, and an acknowledgment logo also change. Existing scientific figures retain their plots, axes, and legends.

improvement.justification: v2 improves qualification through explicit scaling limitations and the approximation sign in Equation (7). However, its added LNS tables lack experimental context and a clear connection to Mix-LN, with conflicting OLMO/LLaMA labels in Table 2. Since the original evidence is otherwise unchanged, these benefits and reporting ambiguities do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
